def inc (e : Nat × Nat) (v : Nat) : Bool := decide (e.1 = v ∨ e.2 = v)

def cnt : Nat → (Nat → Bool) → Nat
  | 0, _ => 0
  | k + 1, p => cnt k p + (if p k = true then 1 else 0)

def occ (n : Nat) (E : Nat → Nat × Nat) (i : Nat) : Nat := cnt n (fun v => inc (E i) v)

def Sat (n m : Nat) (E : Nat → Nat × Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ x : Nat → Bool, ∀ v, v < n → cnt m (fun i => inc (E i) v && x i) = 1

def PM (n m : Nat) (E : Nat → Nat × Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ M : Nat → Bool, (∀ v, v < n → ∃ i, i < m ∧ inc (E i) v = true ∧ M i = true) ∧
    (∀ v, v < n → ∀ i j, i < m → j < m → inc (E i) v = true → inc (E j) v = true → M i = true → M j = true → i = j)

theorem cp (a b : Nat) (hab : a ≠ b) (k : Nat) :
    cnt k (fun v => decide (a = v ∨ b = v)) = (if a < k then 1 else 0) + (if b < k then 1 else 0) := by
  induction k with
  | zero => simp [cnt]
  | succ k ih =>
    simp only [cnt, ih, decide_eq_true_eq]
    repeat' split
    all_goals omega

theorem cnz (p : Nat → Bool) (k : Nat) : cnt k p ≠ 0 → ∃ i, i < k ∧ p i = true := by
  induction k with
  | zero => intro h; simp [cnt] at h
  | succ k ih =>
    intro h
    simp only [cnt] at h
    by_cases hk : p k = true
    · exact ⟨k, Nat.lt_succ_self k, hk⟩
    · have h0 : cnt k p ≠ 0 := by
        intro h0; apply h; simp [hk, h0]
      obtain ⟨i, hi, hpi⟩ := ih h0
      exact ⟨i, by omega, hpi⟩

theorem cpos (p : Nat → Bool) (k : Nat) : ∀ j, j < k → p j = true → 1 ≤ cnt k p := by
  induction k with
  | zero => intro j hj _; omega
  | succ k ih =>
    intro j hj hp
    simp only [cnt]
    by_cases hjk : j < k
    · have := ih j hjk hp
      omega
    · have hpk : p k = true := by
        have : j = k := by omega
        rw [← this]; exact hp
      have h1 : (if p k = true then 1 else 0) = 1 := by simp [hpk]
      omega

theorem ctwo (p : Nat → Bool) (k : Nat) : ∀ i j, i < k → j < k → i ≠ j → p i = true → p j = true → 2 ≤ cnt k p := by
  induction k with
  | zero => intro i j hi _ _ _ _; omega
  | succ k ih =>
    intro i j hi hj hij hpi hpj
    simp only [cnt]
    by_cases hik : i = k
    · have h1 := cpos p k j (by omega) hpj
      have hpk : p k = true := by rw [← hik]; exact hpi
      have h2 : (if p k = true then 1 else 0) = 1 := by simp [hpk]
      omega
    · by_cases hjk : j = k
      · have h1 := cpos p k i (by omega) hpi
        have hpk : p k = true := by rw [← hjk]; exact hpj
        have h2 : (if p k = true then 1 else 0) = 1 := by simp [hpk]
        omega
      · have h1 := ih i j (by omega) (by omega) hij hpi hpj
        omega

theorem cle (p : Nat → Bool) (k : Nat) : (∀ i j, i < k → j < k → p i = true → p j = true → i = j) → cnt k p ≤ 1 := by
  induction k with
  | zero => intro _; simp [cnt]
  | succ k ih =>
    intro hu
    simp only [cnt]
    have hc := ih (fun i j hi hj hp hq => hu i j (by omega) (by omega) hp hq)
    by_cases hpk : p k = true
    · have h0 : cnt k p = 0 := by
        by_cases hz : cnt k p = 0
        · exact hz
        · obtain ⟨i, hi, hpi⟩ := cnz p k hz
          have := hu i k (by omega) (by omega) hpi hpk
          omega
      have h1 : (if p k = true then 1 else 0) = 1 := by simp [hpk]
      omega
    · have h1 : (if p k = true then 1 else 0) = 0 := by simp [hpk]
      omega

theorem phi_occ_and_sat_iff_pm (n m : Nat) (E : Nat → Nat × Nat)
    (hloop : ∀ i, i < m → (E i).1 ≠ (E i).2 ∧ (E i).1 < n ∧ (E i).2 < n)
    (hcubic : ∀ v, v < n → cnt m (fun i => inc (E i) v) = 3) :
    (∀ i, i < m → occ n E i = 2) ∧ (Sat n m E ↔ PM n m E) := by
  constructor
  · intro i hi
    have h := hloop i hi
    have hc := cp (E i).1 (E i).2 h.1 n
    rw [if_pos h.2.1, if_pos h.2.2] at hc
    simp only [occ, inc]
    omega
  · unfold Sat PM
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨x, hx⟩
      refine ⟨x, ?_, ?_⟩
      · intro v hv
        have hne : cnt m (fun i => inc (E i) v && x i) ≠ 0 := by
          rw [hx v hv]; decide
        obtain ⟨i, hi, hpi⟩ := cnz _ m hne
        simp only [Bool.and_eq_true] at hpi
        exact ⟨i, hi, hpi.1, hpi.2⟩
      · intro v hv i j hi hj hiv hjv hMi hMj
        by_cases hij : i = j
        · exact hij
        · have h2 := ctwo (fun l => inc (E l) v && x l) m i j hi hj hij
            (by simp [hiv, hMi]) (by simp [hjv, hMj])
          rw [hx v hv] at h2
          omega
    · rintro ⟨M, hcov, huniq⟩
      refine ⟨M, fun v hv => ?_⟩
      obtain ⟨i, hi, hiv, hMi⟩ := hcov v hv
      have hle := cle (fun l => inc (E l) v && M l) m (fun a b ha hb hpa hpb => by
        simp only [Bool.and_eq_true] at hpa hpb
        exact huniq v hv a b ha hb hpa.1 hpb.1 hpa.2 hpb.2)
      have hge := cpos (fun l => inc (E l) v && M l) m i hi (by simp [hiv, hMi])
      omega

No extra hypothesis weakens the statement.

statement: For every finite loopless cubic multigraph G, let Phi(G) be the positive 1-in-3 formula with one variable per edge of G and one clause per vertex listing its three incident edge variables. Then every variable of Phi(G) occurs in exactly 2 clauses, and Phi(G) is satisfiable if and only if G has a perfect matching. Proof: a satisfying assignment marks a set of edges such that each vertex has exactly one marked incident edge, which is the definition of a perfect matching (loopless, so no edge counts twice at a vertex).

statement: For positive 1-in-3 clause sets, sat and cons3 depend only on the set of distinct nonzero incidence-column types. Variables with identical columns (twins, which lie in the same clauses) can be merged into one type variable T with Y_t in {0,1}. cons3: GF(3) solvability of A x = 1 is unchanged by duplicating a column. sat: each clause contains exactly one true variable, so the copies of a type contribute Y_t <= 1, and any copy can carry Y_t = 1. Consequence for Q-49d9cb2e75: multiplicities are irrelevant, so the rank-4 finiteness reduction only needs the set of column types, at most 15 nonzero types in GF(2)^4.

statement: D-018 FORMALLY VERIFIED (owner 2026-11-19: to be carried as a formally verified result). Two-value criterion: a positive 1-in-3 formula on n variables (each clause three distinct variables) is satisfiable iff A x = 1 has a solution over GF(3) that uses at most two distinct values. Lean 4.35 kernel accepted theorem one_in_three_two_value (core Lean, no Mathlib), axioms propext + Quot.sound only, lab run 454de9fe-13ee-42a6-ae75-e3cb730c1c42, checked file sha256 8ae41a9d24fac990fca3435cde7f87c05a09b01dec8c808b950410a600ec5d5e (artifact:8ae41a9d....lean); fidelity review MATCH (claim:28014452c616 = T44 Lemma C1). Proof idea in the file: for two values {a,b}, the indicator of a suitable t in {a,b} is a Boolean solution (key_choice). Contribution to P vs NP: an EXACT reformulation, not a lower bound - its value depends on which consequences can be proved (see the question below).

question: WHAT FOLLOWS PROVABLY FROM D-018 (formally verified two-value criterion)? Settle each as a theorem with proof (Lean where feasible) or a precise refutation: (1) EXACT PLACEMENT: positive 1-in-3-SAT is polynomially equivalent to TWO-VALUED-COSET over GF(3) (given A and a particular solution y: does y + ker A contain a vector with <= 2 distinct values?) - hence TWO-VALUED-COSET is NP-complete; relate it to the known NP-hard coset problems of coding theory (Berlekamp-McEliece-van Tilborg 1978, from memory - verify). (2) UPPER BOUND (P = NP side): with translation symmetry (x -> x + c*1 keeps the coset), testing the 3^(d-1) representatives decides SAT in 3^(d-1) * poly, d = dim_GF(3) ker A; polynomial whenever d = O(log n); the formally verified nullity-1 criterion (claim:0d815f785160) is d = 1. State and prove the general bound. (3) WHERE HARDNESS MUST LIVE (P != NP side): every hard family must have GF(3) nullity d = omega(log n); measure, on the controls (2-SAT, Horn, XOR-SAT, matching) and on 1-in-3, how the two-valuedness test behaves - is 'coset two-valuedness with large d' a quantitative invariant that is provably polynomial on the controls and superpolynomial on 1-in-3 (filter of the central question)? (4) What D-018 does NOT give: no lower bound for any general model by itself.

evidence.caveat: kernel-checked Lean statement; the fidelity verdict is an independent quality control by a model, NOT a formal proof of equivalence
evidence.checked_file:
def dot : List Nat → List Nat → Nat
  | [], _ => 0
  | _ :: _, [] => 0
  | w :: ws, b :: bs => w * b + dot ws bs

def total : List Nat → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | w :: ws => w + total ws

theorem dot_le_total (w : List Nat) : ∀ (s : List Nat), (∀ b ∈ s, b ≤ 1) → dot w s ≤ total w := by
  induction w with
  | nil =>
    intro s _
    simp [dot, total]
  | cons x xs ih =>
    intro s hs
    cases s with
    | nil => simp [dot, total]
    | cons b bs =>
      have hb : b ≤ 1 := hs b (by simp)
      have hrest : ∀ c ∈ bs, c ≤ 1 := fun c hc => hs c (by simp [hc])
      have h1 : x * b ≤ x := by
        have hcase : b = 0 ∨ b = 1 := by omega
        rcases hcase with h | h <;> subst h <;> simp
      have h2 := ih bs hrest
      simp only [dot, total]
      omega

theorem subset_sum_mod_iff (w : List Nat) (t M : Nat) (ht : t ≤ total w) (hM0 : 0 < M) (hMt : t < M) (hMS : total w - t < M) : (∃ s : List Nat, s.length = w.length ∧ (∀ b ∈ s, b = 0 ∨ b = 1) ∧ dot w s % M = t % M) ↔ (∃ s : List Nat, s.length = w.length ∧ (∀ b ∈ s, b = 0 ∨ b = 1) ∧ dot w s = t) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨s, hlen, hb, hmod⟩
    refine ⟨s, hlen, hb, ?_⟩
    have hle : dot w s ≤ total w := dot_le_total w s (fun b hb' => by rcases hb b hb' with h | h <;> omega)
    have hlt : t % M = t := Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hMt
    have hdm : dot w s % M = t := by rw [hmod, hlt]
    have key : dot w s % M + M * (dot w s / M) = dot w s := Nat.mod_add_div (dot w s) M
    rw [hdm] at key
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (dot w s / M) with h0 | hpos
    · rw [h0, Nat.mul_zero] at key
      omega
    · obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ : ∃ k, dot w s / M = k + 1 := ⟨dot w s / M - 1, by omega⟩
      rw [hk, Nat.mul_add, Nat.mul_one] at key
      omega
  · rintro ⟨s, hlen, hb, heq⟩
    exact ⟨s, hlen, hb, by rw [heq]⟩

#print axioms subset_sum_mod_iff
evidence.fidelity_reason: The Lean theorem `subset_sum_mod_iff` quantifies over all `w : List Nat` and over `s` with `s.length = w.length` and entries in {0,1}, matching s ∈ {0,1}^n. Its hypotheses `t ≤ total w`, `t < M`, and `total w - t < M` (with `0 < M` redundant) are exactly the claim's `0 ≤ t ≤ Σw` and `M > max(t, Σw − t)`, with no extra assumption. The conclusion is the iff between `dot w s % M = t % M` (the congruence, since `t < M`) and `dot w s = t`, with both directions present. Nothing in the claim is unformalised. Not checked here: the proof itself, which the kernel accepted.

def tbl (tt : Nat → Bool) (n m : Nat) : List Bool :=
  (List.range (2 ^ n)).map (fun a => tt (Nat.lor a m))

def popcF : Nat → Nat → Nat
  | 0, _ => 0
  | f + 1, m => m % 2 + popcF f (m / 2)

def dedupF {α : Type} [BEq α] : Nat → List α → List α
  | 0, _ => []
  | _ + 1, [] => []
  | f + 1, x :: xs => x :: dedupF f (xs.filter (fun y => !(y == x)))

def Dk (tt : Nat → Bool) (n k : Nat) : Nat :=
  (dedupF (2 ^ n) (((List.range (2 ^ n)).filter (fun m => popcF n m == k)).map (fun m => tbl tt n m))).length

theorem filt_len {α : Type} (p : α → Bool) : ∀ l : List α, (l.filter p).length ≤ l.length
  | [] => Nat.le_refl 0
  | x :: xs => by
    have ih := filt_len p xs
    simp only [List.filter]
    split <;> simp only [List.length_cons] <;> omega

theorem dedupF_len {α : Type} [BEq α] : ∀ (f : Nat) (l : List α), (dedupF f l).length ≤ l.length
  | 0, l => by simp [dedupF]
  | _ + 1, [] => by simp [dedupF]
  | f + 1, x :: xs => by
    have ih := dedupF_len f (xs.filter (fun y => !(y == x)))
    have h2 := filt_len (fun y => !(y == x)) xs
    simp only [dedupF, List.length_cons]
    omega

theorem dk_le_two_pow (tt : Nat → Bool) (n k : Nat) : Dk tt n k ≤ 2 ^ n := by
  unfold Dk
  have h1 := dedupF_len (2 ^ n) (((List.range (2 ^ n)).filter (fun m => popcF n m == k)).map (fun m => tbl tt n m))
  have h2 := filt_len (fun m => popcF n m == k) (List.range (2 ^ n))
  rw [List.length_map] at h1
  rw [List.length_range] at h2
  omega

evidence.checked_file:
def InRange (n j : Nat) : Prop := 1 ≤ j ∧ j ≤ n

def WF (n : Nat) (c : Nat × Nat × Nat) : Prop :=
  InRange n c.1 ∧ InRange n c.2.1 ∧ InRange n c.2.2 ∧
  c.1 ≠ c.2.1 ∧ c.1 ≠ c.2.2 ∧ c.2.1 ≠ c.2.2

def sum3 (v : Nat → Nat) (c : Nat × Nat × Nat) : Nat :=
  (v c.1 + v c.2.1 + v c.2.2) % 3

def ind (u : Nat → Nat) (j : Nat) : Nat := if u j = 1 then 1 else 0

def cnt (u : Nat → Nat) (c : Nat × Nat × Nat) : Nat :=
  ind u c.1 + ind u c.2.1 + ind u c.2.2

def SatMod3 (n : Nat) (F : List (Nat × Nat × Nat)) (v : Nat → Nat) : Prop :=
  (∀ j, InRange n j → v j < 3) ∧
  (∃ a b : Nat, a < 3 ∧ b < 3 ∧ ∀ j, InRange n j → v j = a ∨ v j = b) ∧
  ∀ c ∈ F, sum3 v c = 1

def OneInThree (n : Nat) (F : List (Nat × Nat × Nat)) (u : Nat → Nat) : Prop :=
  (∀ j, InRange n j → u j = 0 ∨ u j = 1) ∧
  ∀ c ∈ F, cnt u c = 1

theorem pnp_ind (u : Nat → Nat) (j : Nat) (h : u j = 0 ∨ u j = 1) :
    ind u j = u j := by
  unfold ind
  rcases h with h | h <;> simp [h]

theorem pnp_cnt (u : Nat → Nat) (c : Nat × Nat × Nat)
    (h1 : u c.1 = 0 ∨ u c.1 = 1) (h2 : u c.2.1 = 0 ∨ u c.2.1 = 1)
    (h3 : u c.2.2 = 0 ∨ u c.2.2 = 1) :
    cnt u c = u c.1 + u c.2.1 + u c.2.2 := by
  unfold cnt
  rw [pnp_ind u c.1 h1, pnp_ind u c.2.1 h2, pnp_ind u c.2.2 h3]

theorem pnp_key (p q r s t : Nat) (hp : p = s ∨ p = t) (hq : q = s ∨ q = t)
    (hr : r = s ∨ r = t) (hd : (t + 3 - s) % 3 = 1) (hs : (p + q + r) % 3 = 1) :
    ((p + 3 - s) % 3 = 0 ∨ (p + 3 - s) % 3 = 1) ∧
    ((q + 3 - s) % 3 = 0 ∨ (q + 3 - s) % 3 = 1) ∧
    ((r + 3 - s) % 3 = 0 ∨ (r + 3 - s) % 3 = 1) ∧
    (p + 3 - s) % 3 + (q + 3 - s) % 3 + (r + 3 - s) % 3 = 1 := by
  rcases hp with hp | hp <;> rcases hq with hq | hq <;> rcases hr with hr | hr <;>
    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> omega

theorem pnp_shift (n : Nat) (F : List (Nat × Nat × Nat)) (v : Nat → Nat) (s t : Nat)
    (hW : ∀ c ∈ F, WF n c)
    (hval : ∀ j, InRange n j → v j = s ∨ v j = t)
    (hd : (t + 3 - s) % 3 = 1)
    (hF : ∀ c ∈ F, sum3 v c = 1) :
    OneInThree n F (fun j => (v j + 3 - s) % 3) := by
  unfold OneInThree
  constructor
  · intro j hj
    show (v j + 3 - s) % 3 = 0 ∨ (v j + 3 - s) % 3 = 1
    rcases hval j hj with h | h <;> omega
  · intro c hc
    have hW' := hW c hc
    unfold WF at hW'
    obtain ⟨hx, hy, hz, -, -, -⟩ := hW'
    have hs := hF c hc
    unfold sum3 at hs
    obtain ⟨h1, h2, h3, hsum⟩ := pnp_key (v c.1) (v c.2.1) (v c.2.2) s t
      (hval _ hx) (hval _ hy) (hval _ hz) hd hs
    rw [pnp_cnt (fun j => (v j + 3 - s) % 3) c h1 h2 h3]
    exact hsum

theorem pnp001_g0059 (n : Nat) (F : List (Nat × Nat × Nat))
    (hW : ∀ c ∈ F, WF n c) :
    (∃ v, SatMod3 n F v) ↔ (∃ u, OneInThree n F u) := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := h
    unfold SatMod3 at hv
    obtain ⟨_, ⟨a, b, ha, hb, hval⟩, hF⟩ := hv
    by_cases h1 : (b + 3 - a) % 3 = 1
    · exact ⟨fun j => (v j + 3 - a) % 3, pnp_shift n F v a b hW hval h1 hF⟩
    · by_cases h2 : (a + 3 - b) % 3 = 1
      · exact ⟨fun j => (v j + 3 - b) % 3,
          pnp_shift n F v b a hW (fun j hj => Or.comm.mp (hval j hj)) h2 hF⟩
      · have hab : a = b := by omega
        refine ⟨fun _ => 0, ?_⟩
        unfold OneInThree
        refine ⟨fun _ _ => Or.inl rfl, ?_⟩
        intro c hc
        exfalso
        have hW' := hW c hc
        unfold WF at hW'
        obtain ⟨hx, hy, hz, -, -, -⟩ := hW'
        have hs := hF c hc
        unfold sum3 at hs
        rcases hval _ hx with h3 | h3 <;> rcases hval _ hy with h4 | h4 <;>
          rcases hval _ hz with h5 | h5 <;> omega
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := h
    unfold OneInThree at hu
    obtain ⟨hu01, hC⟩ := hu
    refine ⟨u, ?_⟩
    unfold SatMod3
    refine ⟨?_, ⟨0, 1, by decide, by decide, hu01⟩, ?_⟩
    · intro j hj

    · intro c hc

      obtain ⟨hx, hy, hz, -, -, -⟩ := hW'
      have hcnt := pnp_cnt u c (hu01 c.1 hx) (hu01 c.2.1 hy) (hu01 c.2.2 hz)
      unfold sum3
      omega

def clauseSum (x : Nat → Nat) (c : List Nat) : Nat := (c.map x).sum

def satisfies (F : List (List Nat)) (x : Nat → Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ c ∈ F, clauseSum x c = 1

def solvesGF3 (F : List (List Nat)) (x : Nat → Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ c ∈ F, clauseSum x c % 3 = 1

theorem clause_iff (x : Nat → Nat) (c : List Nat) (hl : c.length = 3)
    (hb : ∀ v ∈ c, x v = 0 ∨ x v = 1) :
    clauseSum x c % 3 = 1 ↔ clauseSum x c = 1 := by
  rcases c with _ | ⟨p, _ | ⟨q, _ | ⟨r, _ | ⟨s, t⟩⟩⟩⟩
  · simp only [List.length_cons, List.length_nil] at hl <;> omega
  · simp only [List.length_cons, List.length_nil] at hl <;> omega
  · simp only [List.length_cons, List.length_nil] at hl <;> omega
  · have hp := hb p (by simp)
    have hq := hb q (by simp)
    have hr := hb r (by simp)
    simp only [clauseSum, List.map_cons, List.map_nil, List.sum_cons, List.sum_nil]
    constructor <;> intro h <;> omega
  · simp only [List.length_cons, List.length_nil] at hl <;> omega

theorem oneinthree_gf3 (n : Nat) (F : List (List Nat)) (x : Nat → Nat)
    (hF : ∀ c ∈ F, c.length = 3 ∧ c.Nodup ∧ ∀ v ∈ c, v < n)
    (hx : ∀ j, j < n → (x j = 0 ∨ x j = 1)) :
    (solvesGF3 F x ↔ satisfies F x) := by
  constructor
  · intro h c hc
    have hc' := hF c hc
    have hb : ∀ v ∈ c, x v = 0 ∨ x v = 1 := fun v hv => hx v (hc'.2.2 v hv)
    exact (clause_iff x c hc'.1 hb).mp (h c hc)
  · intro h c hc
    have hc' := hF c hc
    have hb : ∀ v ∈ c, x v = 0 ∨ x v = 1 := fun v hv => hx v (hc'.2.2 v hv)
    exact (clause_iff x c hc'.1 hb).mpr (h c hc)

def sumClause (x : Nat → Nat) (c : List Nat) : Nat :=
  c.foldl (fun acc v => acc + x v) 0

theorem one_in_three_cnf_implies_linear_system_consistent
  (n : Nat) (F : List (List Nat)) :
  (∃ x : Nat → Nat,
      (∀ i, i < n → (x i = 0 ∨ x i = 1)) ∧
      (∀ c ∈ F, List.length c = 3 ∧ sumClause x c = 1)) →
  (∃ x : Nat → Nat,
      (∀ i, i < n → (x i = 0 ∨ x i = 1)) ∧
      (∀ c ∈ F, sumClause x c % 3 = 1)) :=
by
  rintro ⟨x, hx_range, hx_clauses⟩
  refine ⟨x, hx_range, ?_⟩
  intro c hc
  have hlen_eq := (hx_clauses c hc).1
  have hsum_eq : sumClause x c = 1 := (hx_clauses c hc).2
  have : sumClause x c % 3 = 1 % 3 := by
    simpa [hsum_eq]
  simpa using this

theorem pos131_sat_implies_gf3 :
  ∀ (F : List (List Nat)),
    (∀ c, c ∈ F → c.Nodup ∧ c.length = 3) →
    (∃ x : Nat → Nat, (∀ v, x v = 0 ∨ x v = 1) ∧ ∀ c, c ∈ F → (c.map x).sum = 1) →

  intro F _hdom h

  refine ⟨x, fun v => ?_, fun c hc => ?_⟩
  · rcases hx v with hv | hv <;> omega

    omega

abbrev Sat1in3 (n : Nat) (F : List (Nat × Nat × Nat)) : Prop :=
  ∃ y : Nat → Nat, (∀ i, i < n → y i ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ c, c ∈ F → y c.1 + y c.2.1 + y c.2.2 = 1

abbrev Gf3Solves (n : Nat) (F : List (Nat × Nat × Nat)) (x : Nat → Nat) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, i < n → x i < 3) ∧ ∀ c, c ∈ F → (x c.1 + x c.2.1 + x c.2.2) % 3 = 1

abbrev TwoValues (n : Nat) (x : Nat → Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ p q : Nat, p ≠ q ∧ (∀ i, i < n → x i = p ∨ x i = q) ∧ (∃ i, i < n ∧ x i = p) ∧ (∃ j, j < n ∧ x j = q)

def ind (a b : Nat) : Nat := if a = b then 1 else 0

theorem ind_le (a b : Nat) : ind a b ≤ 1 := by
  unfold ind
  split <;> omega

theorem onein3_fiber_iff (n : Nat) (F : List (Nat × Nat × Nat))
    (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hF : F ≠ [])
    (hvars : ∀ c, c ∈ F → c.1 < n ∧ c.2.1 < n ∧ c.2.2 < n)
    (hdist : ∀ c, c ∈ F → c.1 ≠ c.2.1 ∧ c.1 ≠ c.2.2 ∧ c.2.1 ≠ c.2.2) :
    Sat1in3 n F ↔ ∃ x : Nat → Nat, Gf3Solves n F x ∧ TwoValues n x := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨y, hy01, hy⟩
    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ : ∃ c, c ∈ F := by
      cases F with
      | nil => exact absurd rfl hF
      | cons d rest => exact ⟨d, by simp⟩
    have hv := hvars c hc
    have hsum := hy c hc
    have b1 := hy01 c.1 hv.1
    have b2 := hy01 c.2.1 hv.2.1
    have b3 := hy01 c.2.2 hv.2.2
    have key1 : y c.1 = 1 ∨ y c.2.1 = 1 ∨ y c.2.2 = 1 := by omega
    have key0 : y c.1 = 0 ∨ y c.2.1 = 0 ∨ y c.2.2 = 0 := by omega
    have hex1 : ∃ j, j < n ∧ y j = 1 := by
      rcases key1 with h | h | h
      · exact ⟨c.1, hv.1, h⟩
      · exact ⟨c.2.1, hv.2.1, h⟩
      · exact ⟨c.2.2, hv.2.2, h⟩
    have hex0 : ∃ i, i < n ∧ y i = 0 := by
      rcases key0 with h | h | h
      · exact ⟨c.1, hv.1, h⟩
      · exact ⟨c.2.1, hv.2.1, h⟩
      · exact ⟨c.2.2, hv.2.2, h⟩
    refine ⟨y, ⟨fun i hi => by have := hy01 i hi; omega, fun d hd => by have := hy d hd; omega⟩, 0, 1, by decide, fun i hi => by have := hy01 i hi; omega, hex0, hex1⟩
  · rintro ⟨x, ⟨hx3, hcl⟩, p, q, hpq, hall, ⟨i, hi, hpi⟩, ⟨j, hj, hqj⟩⟩
    have hp3 : p < 3 := by have := hx3 i hi; omega

    have hp' : p = 0 ∨ p = 1 ∨ p = 2 := by omega
    have hq' : q = 0 ∨ q = 1 ∨ q = 2 := by omega

    have a3 := hall d.2.2 h3

theorem g0084_lemA (a b c p q : Nat) (hp : p < 3) (hq : q < 3) (hpq : p ≠ q)
    (hd : (q + 3 - p) % 3 = 1)
    (ha : a = p ∨ a = q) (hb : b = p ∨ b = q) (hc : c = p ∨ c = q)
    (hs : (a + b + c) % 3 = 1) :
    (if a = q then 1 else 0) + (if b = q then 1 else 0) + (if c = q then 1 else 0) = 1 := by
  by_cases h1 : a = q <;> by_cases h2 : b = q <;> by_cases h3 : c = q <;>
    simp [h1, h2, h3] <;> omega

theorem g0084_lemB (a b c p q : Nat) (hp : p < 3) (hq : q < 3) (hpq : p ≠ q)
    (hd : (q + 3 - p) % 3 = 2)
    (ha : a = p ∨ a = q) (hb : b = p ∨ b = q) (hc : c = p ∨ c = q)
    (hs : (a + b + c) % 3 = 1) :
    (if a = p then 1 else 0) + (if b = p then 1 else 0) + (if c = p then 1 else 0) = 1 := by
  by_cases h1 : a = p <;> by_cases h2 : b = p <;> by_cases h3 : c = p <;>
    simp [h1, h2, h3] <;> omega

theorem g0084_affine_gf3_two_values_iff_1in3
    (n : Nat) (hn : 3 ≤ n)
    (F : List (Nat × Nat × Nat))
    (hne : F ≠ [])
    (hnodup : F.Nodup)
    (hrange : ∀ c ∈ F, c.1 < n ∧ c.2.1 < n ∧ c.2.2 < n)
    (hdist : ∀ c ∈ F, c.1 ≠ c.2.1 ∧ c.1 ≠ c.2.2 ∧ c.2.1 ≠ c.2.2) :
    (∃ x : Nat → Nat,
        (∀ c ∈ F, (x c.1 + x c.2.1 + x c.2.2) % 3 = 1) ∧
        (∃ p q : Nat, p < 3 ∧ q < 3 ∧ p ≠ q ∧
          (∀ v < n, x v = p ∨ x v = q) ∧
          (∃ v, v < n ∧ x v = p) ∧ (∃ v, v < n ∧ x v = q)))
    ↔
    (∃ w : Nat → Nat,
        (∀ v < n, w v = 0 ∨ w v = 1) ∧
        (∀ c ∈ F, w c.1 + w c.2.1 + w c.2.2 = 1)) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨x, hsat, p, q, hp, hq, hpq, hvals, _, _⟩
    have hcase : (q + 3 - p) % 3 = 1 ∨ (q + 3 - p) % 3 = 2 := by omega
    rcases hcase with hA | hB
    · refine ⟨fun v => if x v = q then 1 else 0, ?_, ?_⟩
      · intro v _
        by_cases h : x v = q <;> simp [h]
      · intro c hc
        obtain ⟨r1, r2, r3⟩ := hrange c hc
        exact g0084_lemA (x c.1) (x c.2.1) (x c.2.2) p q hp hq hpq hA
          (hvals c.1 r1) (hvals c.2.1 r2) (hvals c.2.2 r3) (hsat c hc)
    · refine ⟨fun v => if x v = p then 1 else 0, ?_, ?_⟩
      · intro v _
        by_cases h : x v = p <;> simp [h]
      · intro c hc
        obtain ⟨r1, r2, r3⟩ := hrange c hc
        exact g0084_lemB (x c.1) (x c.2.1) (x c.2.2) p q hp hq hpq hB
          (hvals c.1 r1) (hvals c.2.1 r2) (hvals c.2.2 r3) (hsat c hc)
  · rintro ⟨w, h01, hsum⟩
    obtain ⟨c0, hc0⟩ : ∃ c0, c0 ∈ F := by
      cases F with
      | nil => exact (hne rfl).elim
      | cons c r => exact ⟨c, by simp⟩
    obtain ⟨r1, r2, r3⟩ := hrange c0 hc0
    have s0 := hsum c0 hc0
    have e1 := h01 c0.1 r1
    have e2 := h01 c0.2.1 r2
    have e3 := h01 c0.2.2 r3
    have hone : ∃ v, v < n ∧ w v = 1 := by
      by_cases h1 : w c0.1 = 1
      · exact ⟨c0.1, r1, h1⟩
      · by_cases h2 : w c0.2.1 = 1
        · exact ⟨c0.2.1, r2, h2⟩
        · exact ⟨c0.2.2, r3, by omega⟩
    have hzero : ∃ v, v < n ∧ w v = 0 := by
      by_cases h1 : w c0.1 = 0
      · exact ⟨c0.1, r1, h1⟩
      · by_cases h2 : w c0.2.1 = 0
        · exact ⟨c0.2.1, r2, h2⟩
        · exact ⟨c0.2.2, r3, by omega⟩
    refine ⟨w, ?_, 0, 1, by decide, by decide, by decide, h01, hzero, hone⟩
    intro c hc
    have := hsum c hc
    omega

evidence.fidelity_reason: The Lean conclusion is exactly the claimed equivalence. The left side (`∃ x` with every clause sum `% 3 = 1`, values restricted to `{p,q}` with `p≠q`, both attained on `v<n`) is "GF(3) solution taking exactly two distinct values". The right side (`∃ w` with `w v ∈ {0,1}` and every clause summing to 1 over the three distinct variables from `hdist`) is positive 1-in-3 satisfiability. Clauses are given as ordered triples under `Nodup`, but the constraints are symmetric, so this covers the claim's sets of clauses without adding content.

statement: For every n >= 3 and every nonempty set F of distinct weight-3 clauses over variables 0..n-1: there is a GF(3) vector x with x_a+x_b+x_c = 1 (mod 3) for every clause {a,b,c} in F, taking exactly two distinct values, if and only if F has a 0/1 solution (exactly one variable equal to 1 in every clause). Proof: for distinct values a,b in GF(3) write x = a + (b-a) w with w in {0,1}^n. Then sum over a clause equals (b-a) * sum(w) mod 3, so the clause condition is sum(w) = (b-a)^{-1} = (b-a) mod 3 (sum(w) in {0,..,3}). If b-a = 1, this is 1-in-3 on w. If b-a = 2, sum(w) = 2 on every clause, i.e. sum(1-w) = 1, so 1-in-3 on z = 1-w. Both cases give a 0/1 solution of F. Conversely a 0/1 solution w gives x = w, which takes values {0,1} (exactly two values because each clause contains a 0 and a 1). Hence the set of GF(3) solutions using at most two values is nonempty exactly when F is positive 1-in-3 satisfiable.

theorem cons3_one_of_sat (F : List (List Nat))
    (hF : ∀ c ∈ F, c.length = 3 ∧ c.Nodup)
    (hsat : ∃ x : Nat → Nat, (∀ v, x v ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ c ∈ F, (c.map x).sum = 1) :

def SolvableGF3 (F : List (List Nat)) : Prop :=
  ∃ x : Nat → Nat, (∀ v, x v < 3) ∧ ∀ c ∈ F, (c.map x).sum % 3 = 1 % 3

def Sat131 (F : List (List Nat)) : Prop :=
  ∃ a : Nat → Nat, (∀ v, a v = 0 ∨ a v = 1) ∧
    ∀ c ∈ F, (c.filter (fun v => decide (a v = 1))).length = 1

theorem one_in_three_implies_gf3 (F : List (List Nat)) (h : Sat131 F) : SolvableGF3 F := by
  obtain ⟨a, ha01, hF⟩ := h
  have key : ∀ (l : List Nat), (l.map a).sum = (l.filter (fun v => decide (a v = 1))).length := by
    intro l
    induction l with
    | nil => simp
    | cons w t ih =>
      rw [List.map_cons, List.sum_cons, ih]
      by_cases hw : a w = 1
      · simp [List.filter, hw] <;> omega
      · have h0 : a w = 0 := by
          rcases ha01 w with h1 | h1 <;> omega
        simp [List.filter, hw, h0]
  refine ⟨a, fun v => ?_, fun c hc => ?_⟩
  · rcases ha01 v with h1 | h1 <;> omega
  · rw [key c, hF c hc]

#print axioms one_in_three_implies_gf3

theorem onein3_iff_two_valued (n : Nat) (F : List (Nat × Nat × Nat))
    (hF : F ≠ [])
    (hcl : ∀ c ∈ F, c.1 < n ∧ c.2.1 < n ∧ c.2.2 < n ∧ c.1 ≠ c.2.1 ∧ c.1 ≠ c.2.2 ∧ c.2.1 ≠ c.2.2) :
    (∃ x : Nat → Nat, (∀ i, i < n → x i ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ c ∈ F, x c.1 + x c.2.1 + x c.2.2 = 1)
    ↔
    (∃ x : Nat → Nat, (∀ c ∈ F, (x c.1 + x c.2.1 + x c.2.2) % 3 = 1) ∧
      ∃ a b : Nat, a < 3 ∧ b < 3 ∧ a ≠ b ∧
        (∀ i, i < n → (x i % 3 = a ∨ x i % 3 = b)) ∧
        (∃ i, i < n ∧ x i % 3 = a) ∧ (∃ j, j < n ∧ x j % 3 = b)) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨x, hx, hsum⟩
    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ : ∃ c, c ∈ F := by
      cases F with
      | nil => exact absurd rfl hF
      | cons d _ => exact ⟨d, by simp⟩
    have hgf : ∀ c' ∈ F, (x c'.1 + x c'.2.1 + x c'.2.2) % 3 = 1 := by
      intro c' hc'
      simp [hsum c' hc']
    have hc3 := hcl c hc
    have hp := hx c.1 hc3.1
    have hq := hx c.2.1 hc3.2.1
    have hr := hx c.2.2 hc3.2.2.1
    have hs := hsum c hc
    have key : (x c.1 = 1 ∧ x c.2.1 = 0 ∧ x c.2.2 = 0) ∨
        (x c.1 = 0 ∧ x c.2.1 = 1 ∧ x c.2.2 = 0) ∨
        (x c.1 = 0 ∧ x c.2.1 = 0 ∧ x c.2.2 = 1) := by
      omega
    refine ⟨x, hgf, 0, 1, by decide, by decide, by decide, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro i hi
      have := hx i hi
      omega
    · rcases key with ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩ | ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩ | ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩
      · exact ⟨c.2.1, hc3.2.1, by omega⟩
      · exact ⟨c.1, hc3.1, by omega⟩

def dot (C : List Nat) (c : Nat → Nat) : Nat := (C.map c).sum

theorem sum_ones : ∀ C : List Nat, (C.map (fun _ => 1)).sum = C.length
  | [] => rfl
  | _ :: t => by simp only [List.map_cons, List.sum_cons, List.length_cons, sum_ones t]; omega

theorem kernel_nontrivial (n : Nat) (F : List (List Nat))
    (hn : 3 ≤ n)
    (hF : ∀ C, C ∈ F → C.length = 3 ∧ C.Nodup ∧ ∀ v, v ∈ C → v < n) :
    ∃ c : Nat → Nat, (∃ j, j < n ∧ c j % 3 ≠ 0) ∧ ∀ C, C ∈ F → dot C c % 3 = 0 := by
  refine ⟨fun _ => 1, ⟨0, by omega, by decide⟩, ?_⟩
  intro C hC
  have h3 := (hF C hC).1
  simp [dot, sum_ones, h3]

#print axioms kernel_nontrivial

question: H-TIME-001a (scoped claims to PROVE or REFUTE, contract /root/contracts/PNP-001-H-TIME-001-2026-11-19.md). Model: branching over a FIXED variable order, exact residual-state merging via a global memo table keyed by the residual (frontier-clause state), no clause learning. (1) UNSAT invariance: on UNSAT inputs the set of computed residual states - hence W up to O(1) lookups per duplicate - is the same for DFS, BFS and every Round-Robin interleaving; it depends only on the variable order (the per-level width). (2) In-flight duplicates: under Round Robin a duplicate can arrive while its original is unfinished; then RR must wait (H > 0) or recompute (W grows) - so RR is never below DFS in this model. (3) SAT / early stop: RR over k branches has W <= k * min_i W_i (+H) (dovetailing), and there are families where a fixed DFS order needs exponentially more than RR; but some sequential order always matches RR (simulation). (4) With learning (CDCL), order changes W, but every order is bounded below by resolution size. Measure (1)-(3) on blind cores, certified n=8 cores, SAT instances and 2-SAT/XOR controls with the simulator.
test: proof of (1) and (2); explicit family for (3); simulator counts W, H per policy on identical instances

(3) Compare with the CG certificate (compact, checkable) and its discovery cost: same pattern 'small certificate, possibly expensive construction'. Only syntactic/computable states count as algorithm states; semantic residual counts are meaningful for the decision function over the INPUT (clauses), not for a fixed UNSAT formula.

statement: BRIDGE STATUS (owner 2026-11-19, literature-checked): (1) A computation trace is NOT an UNSAT proof by itself (an always-UNSAT program has short checkable traces); it becomes one only together with a proof of the algorithm s correctness. Precise known form: if the correctness of a poly-time algorithm A is provable in the bounded arithmetic PV (S^1_2), then A s UNSAT answers translate into polynomial-size Extended Frege proofs (Cook 1975; Krajicek-Pudlak). An EF lower bound would therefore exclude all poly-time algorithms with PV-provable correctness, not all algorithms. (2) Cook-Reckhow: NP = coNP iff some propositional proof system is polynomially bounded; superpolynomial lower bounds for EVERY proof system give NP != coNP (hence P != NP); a lower bound for one system (PC, EF) does not, since existence of a p-optimal proof system is open. (3) Alekseev, A lower bound for polynomial calculus with extension rule (CCC 2021 version; owner cites 2026 journal version): exponential BIT-SIZE lower bound over Q for the Binary Value Principle 1 + x1 + 2x2 + ... + 2^(n-1)xn = 0 in PC with extension variables (and radical-type rules) - bit-level/coefficient size as the measured resource, not a CNF and not over GF(2). statement: Boundary of the nullity-parameter route to 1-in-3 SAT. For a positive 1-in-3 formula, nullity_3(A) = n - rank_3(A) >= n - m, since rank <= m. statement: Degree transfer from 3-colouring: for a graph G let T(G) be the positive 1-in-3 formula with clauses (x_v1,x_v2,x_v3) for every vertex v and (x_uc,x_wc,y_uwc) with a fresh variable for every edge uw and colour c. (a) T(G) is GF(3)-consistent for every G. (b) T(G) is satisfiable iff G is 3-colourable. (c) Over GF(2) modulo x^2 = x, if the XOR/carry system of T(G) (L = 1+a+b+c, q = ab+ac+bc per clause) has a polynomial-calculus refutation of degree d, then the standard 3-colouring encoding of G (sum_c x_vc = 1, x_vc x_vc' = 0, x_uc x_wc = 0) has one of degree max(d,2): substitute y_uwc := 1 + x_uc + x_wc (affine, degree-preserving); edge L maps to 0, edge q to x_uc x_wc, y^2+y to 0, vertex L to the vertex axiom, vertex q to a sum of the axioms x_vc x_vc'. CONSEQUENCE if (c) holds: the linear PC-degree lower bounds for 3-colouring of bounded-degree graphs over every field (Lauria-Nordstrom 2017) give an explicit infinite family of GF(3)-blind positive 1-in-3 formulas with PC degree Omega(n) and, by Impagliazzo-Pudlak-Sgall, PC size exp(Omega(n)) in the XOR/carry encoding over GF(2) - a class result for PC/Groebner-based procedures, not P != NP. statement: Exact lemma (short proof): for a positive 1-in-3 clause set S, sat(S)=1 iff the GF(3) affine solution set of A x = 1 contains a 0/1 vector. Proof: a 0/1 solution of the integer system satisfies the GF(3) system. Conversely, a 0/1 vector with every clause sum congruent to 1 mod 3 has clause sum 1, because a sum of three bits lies in {0,1,2,3}. So the non-linear question is membership of {0,1}^n in an exact affine GF(3) space. For n=6 with rank3=5 the solution set has exactly 3 points, so the 0/1 test is a 3-candidate check. Mechanism for the counterexamples: cons3=1 and sat=0 occur exactly when none of the 3 points is 0/1.
